newsitem.title: FRANCE: Danone seeks 100 bln Fr sales by 2000/2005.
newsitem.headline: Danone seeks 100 bln Fr sales by 2000/2005.

text.p: French food group Groupe Danone hopes to achieve annual sales of a hundred billion francs by the year 2000-2005, 40 percent of it outside western Europe, chairman Franck Riboud said in a magazine interview published on Friday.

"My goal is for Danone to make around a hundred billion francs in sales by 2000-2005, of which 40 percent outside western Europe. With already 84 billion francs (in sales) in 1996, including 15 billion outside western Europe, this seems achievable," Riboud told French weekly the Revenu Francais.
Asked about recent rumours Anglo-Dutch food to detergent company Unilever NV might make a bid for Danone, Riboud said "If Unilever made a bid, I would seek a white knight,"
Riboud said that board member Michel David-Weill, who heads Banque Lazard, would be a strong help, if needed.
Riboud said that only earnings growth and the size of funds needed to make a bid for Danone were the company's protection from takeover attacks.
He also declined to comment on market rumours Danone might be considering the sale of its glass packaging unit, which has annual sales of 6.3 billion francs.
Riboud said Danone would strive to raise its profitability, notably that of international operations.

"The average operating profit margin for the group stands at 8.9 pecent. It is at 10 percent in France against only six percent for international operations. We must bring the margins of international operations to the average level for the group. And we must bring the overall average to the French level, that is 10 percent," he said.
Riboud also Danone had improved the profit margin of its international operations by one point each year since four years.
